answer: The fable of a thousand overnight agents dies on a delta ladder. Each identity plants a cedar stake on the public ladder, keyed to its funding root. Fees spiral upward: the first stake costs 40, the k-th fake from the same root pays 40+8(k-1). Auditors replay the ladder, burning stakes with repeated keys or rented cedar. A thousand fakes cost 4,036,000 against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent plants one stake, pays 40 once, keeps a full share.
